blocks.text: Check your Word version before you start

Start with the version, because it decides what you can do. Open Word > About Microsoft Word to see your build. Microsoft's Office for Mac release notes list version 16.114.3, build 26102720, dated October 27, 2026. The only Word item in that entry is quality and performance improvements.

The bigger risk is licensing. Microsoft says that from July 13, 2026, some Mac installs can open and print files but cannot edit, save or create new ones. It calls this reduced functionality mode. The known-issues page covers Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS and people who bought Office 2021 or Office 2019 outright.

Office 2019 for Mac reached end of support on October 10, 2023, according to Microsoft Learn. Those two Microsoft pages do not explain how they fit together. Ask your IT team which rule covers your license before a deadline week.

blocks.title: Test before a deadline
blocks.text: Open a copy of a live file. Try to type, save and track one change. If Word refuses to save, fix the license before the file is due.
How much of a lawyer's day Word takes

Word is a daily tool for legal professionals. An Epinion study, cited by Infoware, found that 90% of them use Word every day. That study drew on 227 interviews with staff at private financial and legal firms. The article does not give the study year.

In-House Connect reports that in-house lawyers spend roughly 20% of their time fighting their word processor rather than drafting. That figure came from a LawVu speaker at a webinar. The article does not explain how it was measured, so treat it as a claim, not a benchmark.
Those numbers explain the stakes. Small habits, like hand formatting or careless pasting, add up over a week of redlines. The rest of this page covers the habits that save the most time.
Turn on Track Changes before you edit a redline

Track Changes records every insertion and deletion, so the other side sees exactly what you touched. Turn it on before your first edit, not after. A change made with tracking off looks like part of the original text. Nobody can see it later without a full compare.

items: Open the document and go to Review > Track Changes.
Turn it on with the Track Changes button, or press ⌘⇧E.
Check the view in the Review tab so the marks show on screen.
Make your edits. Each one shows in color or strike-through.
Turn tracking off only when the document is final and you want clean text.

blocks.text: Track Changes is saved with the file, so the next reader sees the setting too. If a document opens in Reviewing mode, the setting is probably already on. The fix is on the linked page: [Word opens in Reviewing mode on a Mac](/for/lawyers/problems/word-opens-in-reviewing-mode).
Accept and reject live in the same tab. Accept keeps a change in the text. Reject puts the old text back. Use Next and Previous to move from one mark to the next, so you do not skip one.

blocks.title: Read before you accept
blocks.text: Accept All is fast, and it is easy to misuse. Read each change first, or accept only the changes you have already checked.
Compare two Word documents to build a redline

Compare builds a redline for you. Open the newer draft, then go to Review > Compare > Compare. Pick the older file as the original and the newer file as the revised. Word writes the differences into a new document with the changes marked.

Compare is only as good as the files you feed it. Check the last version you sent against the version you received, not against a copy you retyped. Put a date and a version number in each file name, so the dialog shows the right pair.

items: Save both versions under clear names, such as the client, the matter and the version.
Under Original document, choose the older draft.
Under Revised document, choose the newer draft, then click OK.
Read the new document from top to bottom before you send it.

blocks.text: Compare has a known issue. Microsoft's known-issues page lists Compare greying out files and gives a workaround. Read that page before you spend time on a dialog that will not respond.

For the full walk through, read [how to compare two Word documents on a Mac](/for/lawyers/problems/compare-two-word-documents-on-mac). The general steps are on [how to compare two documents in Word on Mac](/how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word).
Read a redline in order, not by scrolling

A redline is easy to misread when you scroll through it. Small changes hide between large blocks of text. Start at the top of the document and step through each mark with Next. Word moves you from one change to the next, so none gets skipped.

Here is a worked example. A counterparty changes Business Day to Calendar Day in a payment clause. The edit is one word, and it shows as a strike-through and an insertion. Read the whole clause, because that change can move a deadline that a later clause depends on.

When a redline is dense, open the Reviewing Pane from the Review tab. It lists each change in a column with the author and the type of edit. Click an item in the list to jump to that change in the text. Use it to check one author's markup before you accept anything.
Add a comment to the exact words that raise the question, not to the paragraph around them. The other side then sees the question next to the change it concerns. Vague comments get vague replies.
Word styles for lawyers: stop formatting by hand

Most formatting pain comes from doing things by hand. In-House Connect says manual formatting of each paragraph makes a document hard to maintain. A style fixes that. It holds the font, spacing and numbering for one type of paragraph, so you change it once.

The same article says Format Painter is weak for longer documents. It also says a global change means reformatting each paragraph, one by one. Set up Heading 1, Heading 2 and Body Text once in your firm template, then apply them as you type.

Here is a worked example. A partner asks you to change every clause title to a new font. If the titles use Heading 2, you edit that style once and every title updates. If someone formatted the titles by hand, you hunt through each heading and fix it one at a time. The style route takes a minute. The hand route can take the afternoon.

blocks.title: Apply the style first
blocks.text: Set the style before you type the clause text, not after. Typing into a styled paragraph keeps the layout clean and saves a cleanup pass later.
To see the basics, read [how to apply heading styles in Word on Mac](/how-to/apply-heading-styles-in-word).
Paste from email and PDFs without breaking the layout

Pasted text brings its own fonts and indents. In-House Connect says pasted text can behave unexpectedly, especially with indentation and fonts. That is how one clause ends up in a different font from the rest of the page.

After you paste, click the Paste Options button that appears near the text. Choose the option that keeps the words and matches the surrounding format. You can also use Edit > Paste Special and pick the plain text option. Plain text is the safest choice for a clause copied from an email.
Pasting from a PDF usually brings hard line breaks with it. Remove those breaks before you apply a style, or every line will look like its own paragraph.
Comments that get answered, not lost

Comments carry questions between you and the other side. Add one with Review > New Comment, after you select the words it refers to. The steps are on [how to add a comment in Word on Mac](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-word).
Resolve a comment when the point is settled. Do not delete it. The thread is your record of who asked what and when. Resolve keeps that history, while Delete removes it for good.
Templates and firm forms that stay clean

Infoware says many Word users rely on templates, and firm forms are the usual reason. A template holds the styles, headers and standard clauses, so each new draft starts from the same base. The 50% figure in that article has no named source, so treat it as a rough signal.

To save a form as a template, go to File > Save As, then choose Word Template in the file format list. Word saves it with a .dotx extension. Keep the master form in a read only folder, so people save copies instead of overwriting it. The full steps are in [how to create a template in Word on Mac](/how-to/create-a-template-in-word).
Macros on a Mac: where VBA falls short

Many firms run small macros for numbering, clause insertion or cleanup. On a Mac, those macros can behave differently from Windows. A wordmvp.com comparison says Mac VBA is based on Visual Basic v5. It lacks Split(), non-modal windows, ComboBox RowSource and ActiveX controls.

The same page says hard-coded file paths fail across platforms, and it recommends Application.PathSeparator. UserForms also use different default fonts, Arial on Windows and Geneva on Mac. A form that looks right on Windows can look wrong on your Mac.

blocks.title: Check the age of the advice
blocks.text: The wordmvp.com page covers Word 97 to Word 2002. Current Word for Mac may have closed some of these gaps. Test your own macros on the Word version your firm uses before you rely on them.
Where Lazur fits in a clause review
Lazur helps when you do not know where something sits or what a change means. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask in plain words. Lazur answers out loud and circles the spot on your screen with a label.

When you ask how to do something, Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. It does not click for you, edit your file or operate Word. You make every change. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app.

Lazur runs on macOS only, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available. Dictation is separate. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor, and use snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots for phrases you repeat in every redline.

blocks.text: Privacy and client files
Client documents are sensitive. Check your firm's rules on AI tools before you ask any assistant about a live matter. The decision belongs to your firm, and no tool can make it for you.

Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on the Mac.
Mistakes lawyers make in Word on Mac

items: Editing with Track Changes off, then sending the file as a redline.
Accepting all changes before anyone reads them.
Comparing the wrong pair of files, then reviewing a redline that does not match.
Typing clause numbers by hand, so one insert breaks every number after it.
Using Format Painter across a long agreement and missing spots.
Pasting from email with the sender's fonts and indents still attached.

blocks.text: What to do next

Check your version first, then turn on Track Changes for your next redline. Build one template with styles, so the next draft starts clean. If you want a voice that points at clauses while you work, [download Lazur](/download) and try it on a draft that is not urgent. Plans and the trial are on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Word document?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, explains, guides and drafts text for you to place. It does not click buttons or operate Word for you. You make every change yourself.

faq.question: Why does my Word document open in Reviewing mode?
faq.answer: Track Changes is usually on for that file, so every edit gets marked. Check Review > Track Changes first. The full fix is on the linked reviewing mode page.

faq.question: What if Compare greys out my file?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists Compare greying out files as a known issue, with a workaround, on its known-issues page. Read that page for the current steps before you try again.

faq.question: Which Office versions does this guide cover?
faq.answer: The release notes used here list Word for Mac version 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. Microsoft says some Mac installs of Office 2021 and Office 2019 can lose editing from July 13, 2026. Check your build under Word > About Microsoft Word.

faq.question: Is there a free trial of Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. The 3-day Pro trial starts when you first open the app and does not need a credit card. Plans and trial details are on the pricing page.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur with client documents?
faq.answer: Only after you check your firm's rules on AI tools. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored.

faq.question: Is Lazur available for Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.
